# Lilo

> Lilo is a free, open-source (MIT) browser for macOS built on WebKit, the engine Safari uses, in an app written in Swift and AppKit with a Svelte interface, with no bundled Chromium and no Electron. It has a sidebar with Spaces that each keep their own sign-ins, runs Manifest V3 extensions from the Chrome Web Store, has terminal tabs beside your pages, and includes a local MCP server so AI agents can drive a real browser in their own Space. Lilo is in public beta.

Lilo is for Mac users who live in a sidebar, people leaving Arc or looking for a lighter alternative to Chrome or Safari, developers who want a terminal and localhost next to their docs, and anyone who wants their AI agents (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor or any MCP client) to browse beside them.

- Requirements: macOS 26 or later. It is a Mac app only, with no sync and no mobile app.
- Price: free. No account, no telemetry, no analytics, and the project runs no server.
- Install: download the DMG from https://github.com/Alexays/Lilo/releases/latest/download/Lilo.dmg, or run `brew install --cask alexays/tap/lilo`.
- Moving in: Lilo imports bookmarks, open tabs, history, sign-ins (cookies) and Chrome Web Store extensions from Safari, Chrome, Brave, Edge, Vivaldi, Opera, Arc, Dia, Comet, Chromium, Firefox and Zen, read on your Mac. It never reads passwords.
- AI agents: there is no AI inside Lilo. When you turn it on in Settings, agents connect to its built-in MCP server over a local socket, work in a separate Agents Space signed in nowhere by default, never see private Spaces, and Lilo asks before an agent sends, pays, deletes or publishes anything.
